event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: Because the 10-K was filed in February 2022 – less than two years after the WHO declared COVID-19 a pandemic – time-decay is minimal and recent facts carry full weight.  WEC discloses both realised and prospective impacts.  Realised impacts include project delays (Badger Hollow I), higher uncollectible receivables, and temporary stress in commercial-paper markets.  Forward-looking language warns of further revenue erosion, liquidity strain, supply-chain cost inflation, labour shortages, and construction slow-downs if new public-health orders arise.  The wording is generally specific (naming supply-chain disruptions, bad-debt spikes, labour attrition, capital-market access), although no dollar amounts are provided.  Mitigations – hygiene protocols, remote-work policies, employee surcharges, monitoring efforts – are noted but do not fully offset the breadth of exposure.  Overall, the pandemic remains a material, multi-dimensional risk with medium-to-high severity; snippet scores therefore cluster in the 3-8 range, consistent with the Time Decay Principle for a very recent event.

evidence_list.snippet: The ongoing COVID-19 pandemic has adversely affected, and could continue to adversely affect, our business functions, financial condition, liquidity, and results of operations.

components.reason: Explicitly links pandemic to actual adverse effects already experienced.
Enumerates multiple core areas (business functions, financial condition, liquidity, results).
States impact is ongoing and could worsen (forward-looking aggravator).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Direct, current and prospective harm across several financial dimensions; recent event, no mitigation mentioned.

evidence_list.snippet: The COVID-19 pandemic has adversely impacted the economy and financial markets, which has adversely affected our businesses.

components.reason: Notes macro-economic deterioration tied to pandemic.
Connects macro impact to company-specific adverse effect.
Recency within 0-3 yrs.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Shows realised negative impact channelled through economy and markets.

evidence_list.snippet: However, there are still questions regarding the extent and duration of the COVID-19 pandemic itself.

components.reason: Highlights uncertainty of duration, implying ongoing risk.
No specific impact quantified (mitigating).

evidence_list.snippet: Orders limiting the capacity of various businesses could be adopted in the future depending on how the virus continues to mutate and spread.

components.reason: Specifies potential regulatory shutdowns linked to pandemic evolution.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Forward-looking operational restriction risk; no magnitude offered.

evidence_list.snippet: The resulting effects of any future orders could have a variety of adverse impacts on us and our subsidiaries, including a decrease in revenues, increased bad debt expense; increases in past due accounts receivable balances, and access to the capital markets at unreasonable terms or rates.

components.reason: Details concrete financial channels (revenues, bad debt, liquidity).
Tied to potential pandemic-related government orders.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Enumerates multiple severe financial consequences if restrictions recur.

evidence_list.snippet: The COVID-19 pandemic and any additional related government responses could impair our and our subsidiaries' ability to develop, construct, and operate facilities.

components.reason: Links pandemic to core operational capability (construct/operate).
Forward-looking but plausible impairment.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Highlights potential disruption to capital projects and operations.

evidence_list.snippet: Risks include extended disruptions to supply chains and inflation, resulting in increased costs for labor, materials, and services, which could adversely impact our ability to implement our corporate strategy.

components.reason: Identifies supply-chain disruption and cost inflation as pandemic-related.
Connects to strategic execution risk.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Specific mechanism (supply chain, inflation) threatens strategic goals.

evidence_list.snippet: We may also be adversely impacted by reduced labor availability and productivity as a result of COVID-19 infections, although we have taken precautions with regard to employee hygiene and facility cleanliness, imposed travel limitations on our employees, implemented additional protocols for our field employees who travel to customer premises, provided additional employee benefits, and implemented remote work policies where appropriate.

components.reason: Cites labour shortage/productivity risk from infections.
Lists multiple mitigation steps (hygiene, remote work, benefits).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Labour risk present but partially mitigated by company actions.

evidence_list.snippet: We could also be impacted by possible labor disruptions, employee attrition, and a reduced ability to replace departing employees as a result of employees who leave or forego employment to avoid surcharges imposed on our medical plan or other required precautionary measures.

components.reason: Highlights attrition and hiring difficulty linked to pandemic-related measures.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Specifies HR risks stemming from pandemic policy responses.

evidence_list.snippet: Despite our efforts to manage the impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic, the extent to which COVID-19 may continue to affect us depends on factors beyond our knowledge or control.

components.reason: Acknowledges uncontrollable residual risk.

evidence_list.snippet: Therefore, we are currently unable to determine what additional impact the COVID-19 pandemic may have on our business plans and operations, liquidity, financial condition, and results of operations, but will continue to monitor COVID-19 developments and modify our plans as conditions change.

components.reason: Admits inability to quantify further impact (uncertainty).
States active monitoring (mitigation).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Net neutral after acknowledging monitoring mitigant.

evidence_list.snippet: For example, the timing of the completion of Badger Hollow I was impacted by supply chain disruptions, primarily related to the COVID-19 pandemic.

components.reason: Provides specific, realised project delay due to pandemic.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Concrete evidence of schedule impact; strong aggravator.

evidence_list.snippet: Upon the initial enactment of certain COVID-19 related shelter-in-place orders in early to mid-March 2020, commercial paper markets became more expensive and related terms became less flexible.

components.reason: Shows actual liquidity pressure caused by pandemic measures.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Historical liquidity squeeze illustrates financial-market exposure.
